subject: English
topic: Double Fill in the Blanks (Set W7)

questions.stem: The minister _______ the bill in Parliament, which was later _______ by all party leaders.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Introduce a bill' is the standard political/legal collocation (first presentation in Parliament). 'Endorsed' = formally approved/supported — consistent with unanimous party support. Option B fails: 'rejected by all' contradicts a successful bill passage.

questions.stem: The teacher was _______ with the student's performance and decided to _______ her publicly.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Impressed' (positive emotion) logically leads to 'commend' (praise publicly). All other pairs contradict themselves: 'disappointed → criticise' is internally logical but the sentence's positive tone (decided to ___ her publicly as a reward) fits 'impressed/commend' better.

questions.stem: Despite _______ weather conditions, the cricket match was _______ as scheduled.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Despite adverse conditions' = even though conditions were bad. 'Held as scheduled' = took place on time. 'Despite' signals contrast: bad conditions BUT the match still happened. Options A, B, D all fail: delayed/postponed/cancelled mean it DID NOT happen as scheduled.

questions.stem: The new policy will _______ the process and _______ corruption at the grassroots level.
questions.explanation: D is correct. A good policy simplifies processes and eradicates corruption — both positive outcomes. Options A–C all pair a positive effect with a negative one (or two negatives), which is inconsistent with a policy being positively framed in the sentence.

questions.stem: The summit brought together leaders from around the world to _______ a common framework for _______ climate change.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Develop a framework for addressing' is a standard formal/diplomatic collocation. Note: 'to oppose/fight climate change' is idiomatically odd ('fight/address climate change' is OK but 'a framework for fighting' is less formal). 'Dismiss' contradicts 'brought together leaders' (would they gather to dismiss the problem?).

questions.stem: The government has decided to _______ the age limit for competitive exams and _______ more opportunities for youth.
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Raise the age limit' = allow older candidates to appear (a youth-friendly move); 'create more opportunities' = positive for youth. Both signal a pro-youth policy. Options A, C, D all include a negative action (remove, restrict, eliminate opportunities).

questions.stem: After years of _______ work, the scientists finally achieved a _______ in cancer treatment.
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Relentless work' = persistent, unceasing effort; 'breakthrough' = major scientific advance. This pair is both internally consistent and factually appropriate for scientific discovery narratives. 'Finally achieved' signals the reward for sustained effort — inconsistent with 'casual/minimal/sporadic'.

questions.stem: The journalist's _______ report exposed the _______ practices of the company.
questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Investigative journalism' is the standard term for in-depth reporting that uncovers wrongdoing. 'Corrupt practices' = what investigative journalism exposes. Option C ('critical / unethical') works grammatically but 'critical report' is far weaker than 'investigative report' in journalistic terminology.

questions.stem: The CEO's speech was _______ enough to _______ the confidence of the shareholders despite the recent losses.
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Convincing enough to restore confidence' is the logical pair: a persuasive speech revives shareholder trust despite setbacks. 'Despite the recent losses' signals the speech succeeded against adversity — only 'restore confidence' (recovering lost trust) fits this nuance. 'Coherent' is positive but 'destroy' contradicts.

questions.stem: The ancient manuscript was _______ by experts for decades before its true _______ was established.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Scholarly 'debate' over an ancient manuscript typically centres on 'authenticity' (is it genuinely old?). 'Debated for decades before authenticity was established' mirrors real academic processes. Option D ('ignored / importance') is plausible in meaning but 'importance' is not 'established' — 'authenticity' is the standard scholarly term for what gets established about a manuscript.
